name: Cable Crossover
summary: A standing cable isolation exercise that pulls high-set handles downward across the body to emphasize the lower sternal fibers of the chest.

setup: Attach single D-handles to both pulleys of a cable crossover station and adjust them to the highest setting.
Grasp a handle in each hand, take a step forward into a staggered stance to establish cable tension, and lean your torso slightly forward from the hips.
Set your arms out to the sides with a slight, fixed bend at the elbows, feeling an initial stretch across your chest.
steps: Draw your hands downward and together in a wide, sweeping arc toward your lower abdomen.
Bring the handles together or slightly cross your wrists in front of your hips, actively contracting your chest.
Pause for one second at peak contraction to squeeze the lower pectorals.
Slowly reverse the motion under control along the same arc, allowing your arms to open until you feel a full stretch across the chest.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handles down and together; inhale smoothly as you return to the stretched starting position.
cues: Lock your elbow angle throughout the motion
Lead with the wrists and squeeze the lower chest

common_faults.fault: Turning the fly into a downward press by bending and extending the elbows.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a consistent, slight bend in the elbows from start to finish so movement occurs strictly at the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso back and forth to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Brace your core, keep the staggered stance anchored, and isolate the movement strictly to your chest and shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the cables to hyperextend the shoulders excessively on the return.
common_faults.correction: Control the eccentric phase and stop when your upper arms align with your torso to protect the shoulder joint.

precautions: Do not allow the weight stack to pull your arms behind the plane of your torso uncontrollably.
